title: PCB thermal interference in sensor enclosure
problem: PCB temperature exceeded its operating threshold following a mechanical enclosure redesign during extended sensor operation.
rootCause: The redesign reduced ventilation clearance and moved a heat-generating power component closer to the PCB sensor array.
solution: The team revised PCB placement, increased clearance around the power component, and modified the enclosure ventilation geometry.

validation.summary: Thermal testing completed successfully under the documented extended-operation profile. PCB temperatures remained within the project operating limit.

lessons: Evaluate airflow and local heat sources together whenever enclosure geometry changes. Include extended-operation thermal soak in design verification.

author: Michael Weber

title: Ventilation clearance restored after housing redesign
problem: A packaging update constrained the air gap between the enclosure wall and the sensor PCB, increasing thermal risk.
rootCause: The mechanical tolerance stack did not account for the PCB keepout and airflow path at worst-case assembly conditions.
solution: The design review restored a 4 mm minimum clearance, added a ventilation channel, and documented the PCB keepout as a controlled interface.

validation.summary: Worst-case tolerance review and thermal chamber checks passed on the updated enclosure geometry.

lessons: Treat electronics keepouts and airflow as explicit mechanical interface requirements rather than informal layout guidance.

author: Alex Morgan

title: PCB keepout moved away from power-stage heat source
component: Power stage and sensor input traces
problem: A new sensor board revision showed a localized temperature rise and intermittent analog noise near the power stage.
rootCause: The original layout placed sensitive analog traces and a temperature-critical sensor channel inside the power-stage thermal keepout.
solution: The team moved the analog input routing outside the keepout, widened the copper heat-spreading area, and added a layout review check.

validation.summary: Bench measurements showed lower local temperature rise and stable signal noise across the documented load range.

lessons: Reuse thermal keepout and trace-routing checks across board variants; physical separation can reduce both heat coupling and signal interference.

author: Michael Weber

title: Enclosure gasket compression exceeded tolerance
problem: Several assembled sensor units showed inconsistent cover seating and a small change in sensor response after environmental cycling.
rootCause: The cover stack-up compressed the gasket beyond its preferred range at the tightest enclosure and fastener tolerances.
solution: A thinner gasket and revised fastener torque window are under evaluation. The corrective design has not yet completed durability testing.

validation.summary: Initial fit checks improved, but vibration and long-duration compression-set validation remain open.

lessons: Track gasket compression across the full tolerance stack and validate the seal after environmental and vibration exposure.

relatedIssues.title: Cover seating varies across tolerance extremes

author: Alex Morgan

title: Temperature-cycle calibration offset corrected in firmware
problem: Sensor readings drifted after repeated temperature cycling even though room-temperature calibration remained within tolerance.
rootCause: The compensation table used a single interpolation segment across a range where the sensor response changed non-linearly.
solution: Firmware now uses a segmented compensation curve, stores the calibration revision with the device profile, and rejects out-of-range coefficients.

validation.summary: The revised calibration passed the documented hot/cold cycle sequence and returned readings to the agreed tolerance band.

lessons: Validate calibration across the operating temperature envelope, not only at room temperature, and version coefficients with the firmware release.

author: Sarah Chen

title: End-of-line thermal validation failed at peak load
problem: Units passed functional checks but failed the end-of-line thermal test during the highest-load portion of the production validation cycle.
rootCause: The fixture airflow blocked one enclosure vent, and the test recipe did not match the extended-operation thermal profile.
solution: The fixture was revised to keep vents clear and the recipe was updated. A second production lot is scheduled to confirm repeatability.

validation.summary: Fixture airflow and recipe checks pass in engineering trials. Repeatability across the next production lot is still pending.

lessons: Production fixtures must reproduce product boundary conditions without masking or creating thermal behavior.

author: David Miller

title: Connector pin fit restored with updated tolerance controls
problem: Intermittent sensor disconnects occurred after harness installation on a small pilot build.
rootCause: Connector pin position and board support tolerance combined to create marginal engagement at one assembly extreme.
solution: The team tightened the board support datum, clarified the connector inspection point, and updated the supplier drawing acceptance range.

validation.summary: Pilot assemblies passed continuity checks after vibration screening using the revised inspection and datum controls.

lessons: Investigate the complete mating tolerance chain across board, connector, harness, and assembly fixture—not just the component drawing.
author: Michael Weber

title: Thermal interface material selected for sensor power stage
problem: The power-stage temperature margin varied between early enclosure builds despite consistent electrical load.
rootCause: The initial interface pad selection had variable contact pressure across the enclosure tolerance range.
solution: The team selected a compliant thermal interface material and added a controlled compression feature to the heat spreader.

validation.summary: Thermal resistance checks passed across three enclosure builds and the documented assembly torque range.

lessons: Specify interface material performance together with compression range, surface condition, and assembly controls.

relatedIssues.title: Thermal margin varies between enclosure builds

author: Alex Morgan

title: False rejects reduced by separating fixture and product checks
problem: The pilot line produced a high false-reject rate on sensor continuity checks, slowing assembly investigation.
rootCause: Fixture contact wear and product connector issues were reported under the same test failure code, obscuring the source.
solution: A fixture self-check was added before each batch and the test result now separates contact resistance from product continuity.

validation.summary: The revised pilot process reduced repeat tests and made fixture-related failures independently traceable.

lessons: Separate test-system health from product acceptance criteria so production data can direct the right corrective action.

relatedIssues.title: Pilot test station reports repeated continuity failures

author: David Miller

title: Cold-start sensor offset remains outside acceptance band
problem: A subset of devices reports a temporary sensor offset during the first seconds after a cold start.
rootCause: The initialization sequence reads the temperature channel before the analog reference has stabilized at low ambient temperature.
solution: A delayed sampling strategy is being evaluated. The software change is not yet validated across hardware revisions.

validation.summary: A bench prototype reduces the offset, but cross-revision testing and startup-time impact review remain open.

lessons: Verify sensor initialization timing against hardware settling behavior at environmental extremes before locking calibration logic.

relatedIssues.title: Temporary sensor offset after cold start

author: Sarah Chen

title: Fastener boss creep observed after hot vibration exposure
problem: A small number of sensor enclosures showed a loosened cover joint after combined hot soak and vibration testing.
rootCause: The polymer boss experienced creep under sustained clamp load, reducing fastener preload at the elevated test temperature.
solution: A metal insert and revised boss geometry are being prototyped. Durability validation is not complete.

validation.summary: Early prototypes retain preload in short-duration checks. Long-duration hot vibration testing is pending.

lessons: Assess fastener retention under combined temperature and vibration loads, especially when polymer parts carry sustained clamp force.

relatedIssues.title: Cover joint preload decreases after hot vibration test

author: Alex Morgan

title: Firmware timing baseline prevents calibration race condition
problem: Calibration results varied between runs when diagnostic logging was enabled on the embedded controller.
rootCause: The sampling task and diagnostic task shared an unprotected timing window, occasionally delaying a sensor conversion.
solution: The project locked sampling to a 10 kHz timing baseline and moved diagnostic formatting outside the acquisition path.

validation.summary: Repeated calibration runs remained stable with diagnostics enabled under the documented controller load.

lessons: Keep logging and telemetry out of time-critical acquisition paths; record the timing baseline alongside calibration evidence.
